NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut on Tuesday attacked Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary over the harassment of a minor girl and boy in Jamui, calling for the state government’s dismissal and alleging that “maha goonda raj” was prevailing in Bihar.“The Samrat Choudhary government must be dismissed. It is a government of goons. There is ‘maha goonda raj’ in Bihar,” Raut said while reacting to the incident.The remarks came after a video purportedly showing a minor girl being groped and her male companion being assaulted by a group of youths in Jamui went viral on social media.The incident has triggered a political controversy in Bihar, with Opposition parties questioning the state government’s law-and-order record and its handling of the case.Congress leader Udit Raj also criticised the Bihar government, saying the incident reflected the deteriorating law-and-order situation in the state.Reacting to the viral video, Raj referred to previous cases involving alleged crimes against minors and questioned the government's response to such incidents.“When a murder accused is the CM of the state, it is not difficult to imagine the condition in Bihar,” Raj said, adding that law and order had deteriorated in the state.Congress MP Manoj Kumar described the Jamui incident as “one that shames humanity” and questioned the government's claims about governance and women's safety.Referring to claims that “Ram Rajya” prevailed in Bihar, Kumar asked what kind of governance was in place when an incident such as the Jamui case occurred in the state.He also referred to an earlier statement attributed to CM Samrat Choudhary that he would resign if such an incident occurred. “The current Chief Minister of Bihar used to say that if such an incident came to light, he would resign and step down from his post. MUMBAI: IIT-Bombay placed Prof Suryanarayana Doolla on immediate suspension from his deanship, following continued students' protests on campus for the last three days. Prof Doolla was the dean of administrative affairs. He was accused of abetment of Sahil Wakode's death by suicide. Wakode's family also filed a case of harassment against him under the Atrocities Act. The institute issued a public apology on their social media handle, after students accused them of 'defaming' Wakode, without carrying out a detailed inquiry."We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil," it said. "The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities. In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process," the institute added. The administration also denied the allegations of the director's resignation, after videos of him from the protest went viral.In a mail sent to the campus residents, the institute director, Prof Shireesh Kedare, mentioned, 'the deanship of Prof Suryanarayan Doolla is suspended with immediate effect. Any further action will be taken after investigation'. Doolla has not been suspended from his professorship at the energy science and engineering department.A meeting of the institute's Board of Governors is underway.The students submitted a charter of 18 demands on Sunday night in a meeting with the director and the institute functionaries, which went on for three hours. The director signed the charter. Students pressed on the suspension of Prof Doolla and an apology along with 16 other demands.In the list of demands raised by the students' groups on the campus, the students have demanded an an independent investigation committee, with student representatives and external members recommended by students, suspension of officials who are found guilty after the investigation, a fair compensation for the families.Among the many demands, the students have also sought a code of conduct and sensitisation for professors.The director signed the list of demands on the live recording, though officials refused to comment. An open house with students is expected to be scheduled today.Protests erupted on the Powai campus on Friday night after Wakode, a second-year student of energy science and engineering, ended his life hours after he was caught using a mobile phone during the institute’s mid-semester examination. He allegedly uploaded the exam paper on an AI platform for answers. This is the third case of suicide on the campus this year.While the institute, in a statement, mentioned that no action was initiated against Wakode, many claimed that he was threatened with suspension.
Article Summary: IIT Bombay suspends Dean Suryanarayana Doolla. He was accused of abetment of Sahil Wakode's death by suicide. The students submitted a charter of 18 demands on Sunday night in a meeting with the director and the institute functionaries, which went on for three hours.

Article Title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s big push to make state drug-free
Article Text:
Punjab Chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Punjab Chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann’s government has expanded its ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’ anti-drug campaign beyond a conventional police crackdown, combining action against drug networks with prevention in schools, youth engagement, community vigilance and treatment for people battling addiction.The government said the campaign seeks to make it harder to sell drugs, easier for citizens to report peddling, prevent young people from falling into addiction and ensure those affected can access timely treatment. The strategy brings police, teachers, students, community volunteers and health workers into a coordinated anti-drug effort.Between March 2025 and September 2026, Punjab’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force registered 61,824 FIRs and arrested 81,433 people. Authorities seized 3,918 kg heroin, 991 kg opium, 47 tonnes poppy husk, 1,416 kg ganja and 65 lakh tablets and capsules during the period. Punjab Police also conducted 79,293 public meetings to strengthen community participation in the campaign.The government has simultaneously taken the prevention campaign into schools. A 14-week anti-drug curriculum is being taught to 7.5 lakh students across 3,600 schools through trained teachers.In the first phase, nearly 25,000 teachers from 13 districts are being sensitised, with 7,000 already trained in Amritsar, Tarn Taran and Fazilka. The programme aims to help teachers identify early signs of mental-health distress, vulnerability to substance abuse and possible intervention.Youth programmes are also being used to address peer influence and social acceptance of drugs. Schools have been given year-long activity calendars, while colleges are promoting cultural festivals, mental-health clubs, sports and other activities to encourage healthier lifestyles and reduce the stigma around recovery.At the grassroots level, around 1.25 lakh people have joined nearly 15,000 Village and Ward Defence Committees. More than 50,000 members have been trained to use the Nasha Mukti App to report drug-related information and connect people seeking help with government services.Since its launch on March 1, 2025, the safe Punjab whatsApp helpline has received more than 51,000 citizen tip-offs, which the government said helped police make over 25,000 drug-related arrests.The government has also expanded treatment infrastructure, with Punjab currently having 547 OOAT centres, 219 de-addiction centres and 91 rehabilitation centres. Government facilities have been revamped, health workers trained and skilling and creative activities introduced at treatment centres.Admissions to government de-addiction and rehabilitation centres rose from over 12,200 in 2024 to nearly 34,000 in 2025, an increase of more than 170%, according to the government. The figures indicate a sharp rise in people seeking institutional support as Punjab seeks to combine enforcement with prevention, community action and rehabilitation in its fight against drugs.
Article Summary: Punjab’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force registered 61,824 FIRs and arrested 81,433 people. Authorities seized 3,918 kg heroin, 991 kg opium, 47 tonnes poppy husk and 1,416 kg ganja.

Article Title: Grounds in writing a must during arrests even in UAPA: Supreme Court
Article Text:
Supreme Court Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor

'Court nod required for re-arrest when flouting Article 22'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner, Supreme Court on Monday held that a person's personal liberty cannot be invaded except in accordance with the procedure established by the Constitution, even if accused of a grave offence and anti-social activities, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.Elucidating Article 22 of the Constitution, which offers protection against arrest and detention in certain cases, a bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused. SC said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA - regardless of the nature and gravity of offence.Going a step further, the bench said that if a person's arrest is declared illegal for non-compliance with Article 22, then he or she cannot be re-arrested in the same case without approval from a senior police officer and nod from the court concerned."We need to remind ourselves that Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be interpreted in a vacuum. Interpretation of Constitution cannot also be left to imponderables in the form of ifs and buts.Constitution is based on certain basic principles, much above the statutory threshold. Therefore, violation of Constitution or a constitutional provision cannot be countenanced. It has to be dealt with strictly. It is not dependent on the nature or gravity of the offence, encompassing within its sweep all offences. It cannot be interpreted in a restrictive manner," the bench said. Referring to SC's verdict in the Prabhu Dayal Deorah case on preventive detention, the court said, "The gravity of the evil to the community resulting from anti-social activities can never furnish an adequate reason for invading the personal liberty of a citizen, except in accordance with the procedure established by Constitution and laws."The bench said that when a person is arrested, his right to liberty under Article 21 is curtailed and it is necessary that the person must understand on what grounds he has been arrested."The requirement of informing the arrested person the grounds of arrest in the light of and under Article 22(1) is not a mere formality but a mandatory binding constitutional safeguard. Thus, if a person is not informed of the grounds of his arrest as soon as may be, it would amount to violation of his fundamental rights thereby curtailing his right to life and personal liberty under Article 21 of Constitution, rendering the arrest illegal," the bench said.
Article Summary: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S Chandurkar said a person must be provided with the grounds of arrest by the probe agency at the time of arrest in writing and its language understandable to the accused. SC said this is applicable in all cases including under special laws - such as PMLA and UAPA.

Article Title: ‘PM Modi assured me’: OP Rajbhar’s claim on UP division revives decades-old debate
Article Text:
UP minister OP Rajbhar (File photo)

When Mayawati proposed carving out four states from UP

Why Uttar Pradesh matters

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar has claimed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi assured him that the state would be divided into four parts, reviving a nearly two-decade-old debate over dividing the country's most populous state.Rajbhar, who heads BJP ally Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), claimed that PM Modi told him Uttar Pradesh could be divided after the caste census.“We want to assure you regarding the 27% reservation. I spoke with the prime minister about this,” he told the audience at an SBSP programme in Deoria on Sunday.“He (PM Modi) said, ‘Om Prakash ji, your point is justified, but some people are opposing it.’ I asked him how we could move forward, and he replied, ‘I will conduct a caste census, and once we have counted the castes, there will be no difficulty.’ The state will be divided into four parts. And on the day the Purvanchal is formed, if the chief minister is to be from any caste, then a Rajbhar’s son will become the chief minister,” he added.However, another UP minister and BJP ally, Sanjay Nishad, dismissed Rajbhar’s remarks as “misleading”, saying the Nishad Party was not in favour of a reorganisation.“There had been a demand to divide UP earlier, but now the state is progressing rapidly in all spheres.Further, special development funds have been allocated for regions like Bundelkhand and Purvanchal that needed handholding,” Nishad told PTI.Rajbhar has advocated the division of Uttar Pradesh in the past as well, saying in October 2018 that the “state can be developed only after it is divided into four parts.”With the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due in early 2027, Rajbhar’s remarks have revived the long-running political debate over dividing the state.Ahead of the 2012 UP assembly elections, then chief minister Mayawati revived the demand, with the state assembly passing a resolution to split Uttar Pradesh into Avadh Pradesh, Purvanchal, Bundelkhand and Paschim Pradesh.In 2011, her government had sent a proposal to the Congress-led Centre seeking the creation of the four states.Before that, in 2008, Mayawati had proposed dividing Uttar Pradesh into three parts.Several parties, including the Rashtriya Lok Dal and Congress, have also backed demands for dividing the state at various points. There have additionally been calls for a separate Bundelkhand comprising parts of Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring Madhya Pradesh.Uttar Pradesh was last divided in 2000, when the BJP-led central government carved out Uttarakhand, then known as Uttaranchal.With a population of around 25 crore, Uttar Pradesh is India’s most populous state. If it were an independent country, its population would make it the fifth- or sixth-most populous country in the world.Geographically, Uttar Pradesh is the fourth-largest state in India.It sends 80 members to the 543-seat Lok Sabha, the highest representation of any state or Union territory. Its legislative assembly has 403 members.Six prime ministers were born in Uttar Pradesh, while several others, including Narendra Modi, have represented the state in Parliament.
Article Summary: Uttar Pradesh was last divided in 2000, when the BJP-led central government carved out Uttarakhand, then known as Uttaranchal. With a population of around 25 crore, Uttar Pradesh is India’s most populous state. If it were an independent country, its population would make it the fifth or sixth-most populous country in the world.

Article Title: UK backs Saudi Arabia with RAF Voyager refuelling support amid Houthi campaign
Article Text:
File photo: Andy Burnham

UK links support to energy security

Britain stops short of direct strikes

The UK has stated that it will provide Saudi Arabia with defensive military support, including air-to-air refuelling for Saudi fighter jets, as Riyadh faces a renewed campaign of attacks by Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen.Prime minister Andy Burnham said Saudi Arabia had requested military support and that Britain had agreed to provide an RAF Voyager aircraft to refuel Saudi jets for several weeks.The aircraft is expected to operate from RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. British officials described the deployment as “time limited” and said it was intended to help Saudi Arabia defend its energy infrastructure and keep key oil routes open.The move comes as the Houthis have advanced along Yemen’s Red Sea coast and taken control of the strategically important Bab al-Mandab Strait, a major maritime route connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden.Burnham said the decision was partly driven by concerns over the impact of the conflict on energy supplies and the cost of living in Britain.“I go back to the point I made about cost-of-living pressures and acting to secure the interests of Britain and the wider region,” Burnham told reporters from BBC.Saudi Arabia has faced a series of Houthi attacks in recent days, including missile and drone strikes targeting Riyadh and energy infrastructure along the Red Sea coast.The attacks have raised concerns over further disruption to Saudi oil exports.The UK already provides air-defence support to Saudi Arabia, including the deployment of the Sky Sabre system. The new refuelling mission will allow Saudi aircraft to remain airborne for longer while responding to incoming threats.The deployment is significantly more limited than Britain's previous military action against the Houthis.In January 2024, the UK joined the US in carrying out airstrikes against Houthi military targets in Yemen after the group attacked commercial shipping in the Red Sea. Further British-American strikes followed later that year.This time, the UK has framed its involvement as defensive support rather than direct attacks on Houthi positions.The announcement also comes as Burnham prepares for his first face-to-face meeting with US President Donald Trump at the UN. Burnham said he would urge Trump to work towards ending the war in Iran, arguing that the conflict and the wider instability in the Middle East were contributing to economic pressure in Britain.The UK government is also concerned about the wider consequences of the fighting for global energy and shipping routes. The Bab al-Mandab Strait has become a new flashpoint after the Houthis' recent advances along Yemen's Red Sea coast, while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely disrupted.Burnham said Britain wanted to see the conflict end as quickly as possible and was ready to work with its allies to reduce the wider instability.
Article Summary: UK to provide air-to-air refuelling for Saudi fighter jets. Move comes as Riyadh faces renewed campaign of attacks by Iran-backed Houthi forces in Yemen. Decision driven by concerns over impact of conflict on energy supplies and cost of living.

Article Title: South Korea proposes nuclear freeze with Kim Jong Un in exchange for sanctions relief: Report
Article Text:
South Korea's Lee urges Trump to seek nuclear freeze deal with North Korea (file photo)

Why Lee wants a nuclear freeze first

North Korea has more leverage now

South Korean president Lee Jae Myung has urged US president Donald Trump to seek a nuclear freeze deal with North Korea instead of insisting on immediate denuclearisation, arguing that sanctions have failed to stop North Korea from expanding its weapons programmes.In an interview with the New York Times, Lee said Washington could offer sanctions relief in exchange for Pyongyang halting further development of nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology.“I believe there is significant value in a trade-off between sanctions –– which are not particularly effective anyway –– and a stop to the development of additional nuclear weapons and intercontinental ballistic missile technology,” Lee told NYT.Lee argued that demanding complete denuclearisation under current circumstances would achieve little, as North Korea has continued to expand its nuclear capabilities while strengthening ties with Russia and China.“Aiming for denuclearisation under the current circumstances guarantees that nothing will be accomplished,” he said.Lee’s proposal would make a nuclear freeze the first step, followed by reciprocal incentives and concessions aimed at building trust with Pyongyang.He said the longer-term goal would be to create conditions in which North Korea feels secure enough to eventually reduce and give up its nuclear arsenal.The South Korean president believes Trump is uniquely positioned to restart talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, given the two leaders’ previous personal diplomacy. Trump met Kim three times during his first term, including a 2019 meeting at the inter-Korean border, but those talks failed to produce an agreement.Lee said the alternative to diplomacy was increasingly risky as North Korea continued to expand its nuclear arsenal.“Our estimates suggest that North Korea is now capable of producing, or may already be producing, an additional 10 to 20 nuclear weapons each year,” he said, warning that Pyongyang could eventually be tempted to export nuclear weapons and missiles for money.Lee’s push comes as North Korea has moved closer to Russia and China and become less dependent on negotiations with Seoul or Washington.Pyongyang has deployed troops and weapons to support Russia’s war in Ukraine, strengthening its relationship with Moscow. North Korea has also deepened ties with Beijing, while its economy has shown signs of growth.That has given Kim more room to resist pressure from Washington. North Korea has also continued developing its nuclear and missile capabilities despite Trump’s efforts to revive diplomacy.North Korea has also been regularly carrying out military exercises and testing its arsenal of ballistic missiles near South Korean waters, worsening tensions in a region already plagued by military tensions and a long-running standoff between the two Koreas.Trump had also recently scaled back a major US-South Korean military exercise, describing such drills as hostile toward Kim. North Korea has nevertheless continued weapons activity, including recent ballistic missile launches.Lee is not alone in arguing for a shift towards a phased approach. Stephen E Biegun, who served as the US special representative for North Korea during Trump’s first term, recently said Washington could negotiate a “slowing or freezing” of North Korea’s nuclear arsenal.But North Korea has repeatedly signalled that it does not intend to give up its nuclear arsenal, making any freeze deal potentially difficult to negotiate.Lee nevertheless believes a freeze would be a more realistic starting point than demanding complete denuclearisation at the outset.
Article Summary: Lee Jae Myung argues that sanctions have failed to stop North Korea from expanding its weapons programmes. He argues that demanding complete denuclearisation under current circumstances would achieve little. Lee’s proposal would make a nuclear freeze the first step, followed by reciprocal incentives and concessions aimed at building trust with Pyongyang.

Article Title: Amid Trump’s clash with CNN, Politico, MS NOW, White House launches ‘Trump TV’
Article Text:
White House launches 24/7 ‘TRUMP TV’ amid press access battle

The White House on Monday launched ‘TRUMP TV: The Essentials Station’, a 24/7 digital video stream featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and other content, as the Trump administration faces a legal challenge from CNN, MS NOW and Politico over their exclusion from the White House.The White House said the new service would bring the administration's "biggest moments" together in one place, with content updated in real time. The stream was launched on the White House's YouTube channel at 7 pm ET on Monday.The launch came hours after CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration, seeking to restore their access to the White House. The organisations argue that the administration's decision to revoke their journalists' credentials violates their First Amendment rights.Trump had barred the three outlets from the White House after criticising their coverage. Their reporters were denied entry to the White House grounds on Saturday and had their press credentials confiscated, according to the organisations.CNN was also removed from its scheduled television pool duties. ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC subsequently joined CNN in suspending their participation in the White House television pool after CNN was removed from a scheduled assignment.The television pool normally provides shared video coverage of presidential events to broadcasters and other news organisations. With the pool disrupted, the White House's own video feed has become a more prominent source of footage from presidential events.Trump on Monday sharply criticised the three organisations in a social media post after they sued his administration."As expected, Fake News CNN, Politico (Pay back the 8 Million Dollar contribution made by the U.S. Government to keep them afloat!), and MSNOW (formerly known as MSDNC!), have brought suit to gain access to the White House, and your President, ME! They have drawn a great Judge, for them, a man who ruled in favor of Jim Acosta, who now seems to have disappeared from the Planet. The Judge’s name is Tim Kelly, and he was, sadly, appointed by “TRUMP. ” In other words, almost without question and, as usual, we’ll go for appeal because Fake News people and publications that only write negatively, and who violate our National Security by writing false and defamatory stories with unknown “sources,” shouldn’t be allowed access to the most important Office anywhere in the World. It is called the Oval Office, and it should be treated with Decorum, Respect, and Dignity, not defiled by Third Rate Clowns, who purposefully distort, twist, and degrade with everything they write or publish. Virtually every story about me, or anything having to do with me, is negative, wrong and, in many cases, DANGEROUS for our Country! No matter how GREAT my Achievements, they trivialize and demean. The fact is, I won all seven Swing States, the Popular Vote, the Electoral College (312 to 226), and the Counties throughout America by 86%, and yet it is reported that I get 94% bad publicity. With such a Crooked and Corrupt Press, how did I win in such a LANDSLIDE? It is because the Media has NO credibility, and that is a very bad thing for our Nation! Why should I have to give “access” to such people? Perhaps Judge Kelly could explain that! In any event, I have an obligation to fight for the Success and Safety of our Country. FAKE NEWS IS A THREAT TO DEMOCRACY, and I will do whatever is necessary to make sure that the U.S.A. thrives."The three organisations said their lawsuit was intended to defend their First Amendment rights and the principle that the government should not decide what the press reports."This morning, we notified the government that we are filing a lawsuit today to protect our First Amendment rights and defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports or publishes," the outlets said in a joint statement.The case has been assigned to US District Judge Timothy Kelly, who was appointed by Trump during his first term. Kelly previously handled CNN reporter Jim Acosta's legal challenge after the White House revoked his press access in 2018.CNN, MS NOW and Politico have asked the court to restore their access while the case proceeds. A hearing on their request is scheduled for Wednesday.The dispute centres on whether the administration can restrict journalists' access to the White House based on objections to their reporting. The organisations have argued that their credentials were revoked without notice or a process to challenge the decision.The launch of TRUMP TV adds a new element to the dispute, giving the administration a dedicated digital platform to distribute its own footage and announcements at a time when traditional White House television pool coverage has been disrupted.The White House has described the platform as an "essentials station", featuring top videos, major remarks and highlights from the administration.
Article Summary: The White House on Monday launched a 24/7 digital video stream featuring administration announcements, presidential remarks and other content. The launch came hours after CNN, MS NOW and Politico filed a federal lawsuit against the Trump administration, seeking to restore their access to the White House. Article Title: Pakistan airstrikes on Afghanistan: 3 killed, several injured as conflict fears grow

Taliban warns of 'crushing response'

Kabul denies sheltering TTP

Afghanistan keeps door open for talks

At least three people were killed and several others injured in a Pakistani airstrike targeting Afghanistan's northeastern Kunar province, Tolo News reported on Monday, citing a provincial official.The military strike is supposedly in retaliation for suicide bombing at a police station compound in northwestern Pakistan, raising fears that tensions between the neighbouring nations could once again turn into open fighting.Pakistan and Afghanistan were involved in their most serious military confrontation in years in February. The latest escalation comes days after the Taliban warned that it would defend Afghan territory against any Pakistani military action.Taliban spokesperson Zabihullah Mujahid, ahead of the imminent Pakistani strikes, had warned Islamabad against carrying out strikes inside Afghanistan, saying Kabul would respond militarily if its territory is attacked.In an interview with Al Arabiya English, Mujahid rejected Pakistan's allegations that militant groups based in Afghanistan recruit, train and launch attacks against Pakistan.“If Pakistan invokes Article 51 to violate the sanctity of Afghan territory, Afghanistan has the right to defend its country, and we will do so,” Mujahid said.He said any Pakistani military operation inside Afghanistan would amount to a violation of Afghan sovereignty and could trigger a strong response from Kabul.Mujahid was responding to comments by a Pakistani military spokesperson, who had told Al Arabiya English that militant groups were using Afghan territory to recruit, train and arm fighters before sending them into Pakistan.Mujahid rejected those allegations and said the Taliban administration does not allow the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan , or TTP, to operate from Afghan soil.He also denied that the Taliban government supports armed groups carrying out attacks against other countries. Instead, Mujahid said Pakistan should examine its own internal security problems, arguing that violence involving the TTP and Baloch armed groups existed before the Taliban returned to power in 2021.Pakistan has repeatedly accused militant groups of operating from Afghanistan and has pressed Kabul to take action against them. The Taliban has consistently denied allowing Afghan territory to be used for attacks against Pakistan.Despite his warning of military retaliation, Mujahid said Kabul was still willing to engage with Islamabad through dialogue.He called for stronger intelligence-sharing arrangements and greater bilateral cooperation to address security concerns along the two countries' border.Mujahid also backed a possible mediation role for Saudi Arabia, saying Riyadh has good relations with both Afghanistan and Pakistan and could help the two sides resolve their differences.Relations between Kabul and Islamabad have remained strained over militant activity along their shared border. The latest airstrike, coming amid fresh security concerns, risks further worsening those ties and could lead to another confrontation between the neighbours.

Article Title: What happened after Sahil left exam hall? Cops pieces together CCTV trail in IIT-Bombay student death
Article Text:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch is scrutinising CCTV footage in connection with the death by suicide of IIT Bombay student Sahil Ravindra Wakode





MUMBAI: The Mumbai Police Crime Branch is piecing together CCTV footage from IIT Bombay 's examination hall, campus and hostel to reconstruct student Sahil Ravindra Wakode's movements on the day he died by suicide, with investigators focusing on the sequence of events between the end of his exam and his return to his hostel room, an official said on Tuesday.The Crime Branch clarified that the CCTV footage has not been released or shown to anyone and is currently being examined by the investigating team.According to the Crime Branch, CCTV cameras recorded Sahil's movements inside the examination hall between 12:30 PM and 12:45 PM on September 18.With around 15 minutes remaining for the examination to conclude, Sahil was seen bending down to look at something kept in his pocket.A professor subsequently questioned him and took him aside, away from the other students, according to the police."After leaving the examination hall, Sahil moved across the campus. He reached his hostel room at approximately 1:25 PM. He did not step out of the room thereafter," the Crime Branch official said.Sahil, a second-year BTech student of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found dead in his hostel room later that day.Investigators are now examining footage from different locations on the campus to establish Sahil's movements from the examination hall to the hostel and further piece together the events preceding his death.The development comes amid protests and counter-protests at IIT Bombay following Sahil's death. Security was also stepped up on the campus on Tuesday amid the tensions.IIT Bombay student representatives on Monday said their protest was not intended to justify cheating or academic misconduct, but to raise concerns over systemic issues within the institute and seek institutional reforms.The representatives said they had formulated a comprehensive set of demands, which were formally placed before the director.They said the director acknowledged and signed the demands and agreed to work towards their implementation within specified timelines.On Prof. Suryanarayana Doolla, the students said they had not presumed his guilt or prejudged the ongoing investigation.They said their demand was for Doolla to be relieved of his administrative duties as Dean of Administrative Affairs during the investigation as a precautionary measure.The IIT Bombay PRO clarified that Doolla had only been suspended from the deanship.Earlier on Monday, the IIT Bombay Faculty Forum staged a campus march in support of Doolla. The forum said he was discharging his duties in accordance with the institute's Senate-approved academic policies.According to the Faculty Forum, Doolla, who was the course instructor, was invigilating the mid-semester examination from 11 am to 1 pm on September 18 when he saw a student using a smartphone without authorisation.The forum termed the incident "academic malpractice" and said Doolla reported it to institute authorities as per the approved procedure.Sahil's family has alleged caste-based harassment and sought a thorough probe, including a CBI inquiry. His parents have filed a case under the SC/ST Act, alleging discrimination.The family has also sought access to CCTV footage and other evidence and alleged that several people could be involved in the circumstances leading to Sahil's death.In an earlier statement issued on September 19, IIT Bombay had said the student was caught cheating during an examination and had used a phone to upload the question paper to ChatGPT to seek answers.The institute later issued a formal apology and retracted its earlier characterisations of the incident.The Mumbai Police has officially transferred the case to the Crime Branch.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: Mumbai Police Crime Branch is piecing together CCTV footage from IIT Bombay's examination hall, campus and hostel to reconstruct student Sahil Ravindra Wakode's movements. Investigators focusing on sequence of events between end of exam and return to his hostel room. Crime Branch clarified that the CCTV footage has not been released or shown to anyone and is currently being examined.

Article Text:
MBMC education officer Sulabha Vatare confirmed that a notice has been issued.





BHAYANDER: Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation’s education department has issued a show-cause notice to a Bhayander school following a complaint that it fined a student Rs 50 for carrying a dish made of fenugreek leaves for lunch.According to Robert D’Souza, office-bearer of MNS, which lodged the complaint, a majority of the students of the institute, Tapovan Vidyalaya, belong to the Jain community and parents are reportedly told at the time of admission not to send non-vegetarian food and root vegetables in their children’s lunchboxes.He said imposing the fine amounted to forcing a set of dietary practices on students.MBMC education officer Sulabha Vatare confirmed that a notice has been issued.The notice states that schools cannot impose dietary curbs on students and that imposing a fine for bringing certain food items is a serious matter. Such a practice amounts to a violation of Right to Education (RTE) Act, students’ fundamental rights and state govt rules, it said.TOI attempted to reach out to the school management for a comment.The incident came days after a controversy over Seven Square School in Mira Road, run by BJP MLA Narendra Mehta, issuing a circular asking students not to bring onion, garlic and certain other food items in their lunchboxes during Paryushan. The school, which was also sent a notice, withdrew the circular later.
Article Summary: Mumbai's education department has issued a show-cause notice to a Bhayander school following a complaint that it fined a student Rs 50 for carrying a dish made of fenugreek leaves for lunch. A majority of the students of the institute, Tapovan Vidyalaya, belong to the Jain community.

Article Title: Rohini Jail Murder: Two inmates stab undertrial to death inside Rohini Jail, police probe power struggle
Article Text:
An undertrial was stabbed to death by two inmates inside Rohini central jail (Representative image generated using AI)

Two inmates stab undertrial to death inside Rohini jail

mulaqat





NEW DELHI: A 31-year-old undertrial was allegedly stabbed to death by two other inmates inside central jail no. 10 in Rohini Monday. Both have been arrested.Police are probing whether a battle for dominance inside the prison led to the killing.The deceased has been identified as Pradeep alias Mohinder, who was in judicial custody. Tihar sources said he was involved in more than 10 cases.Pradeep had been in jail since April 2024 in a robbery case and was booked on the charge of common intention under IPC and under Arms Act.The attackers and the victim were lodged in different cells in barrack number 203, and a tussle between them had been going on for a long time, a police officer said.Seven days ago, there was a scuffle between Pradeep and one of the accused, police said. One of the attackers allegedly has four to five cases registered against him.According to preliminary information, Pradeep was returning to his barrack when he was allegedly attacked with a crude, handmade weapon made from jail equipment, suffering a stab injury to his neck.A jail official said Pradeep was attacked around 12.30pm while returning from a(meeting) near the gate of barrack number 203.He was first taken to the jail hospital and later shifted to another hospital, where he was declared dead.According to information received by Samaypur Badli police, doctors at BSA Hospital declared him brought dead.Senior police officers, along with the station house officer, went to the jail and BSA Hospital. Police collected the medico-legal case report and examined CCTV footage from the jail premises. A case is being registered at Samaypur Badli police station.A relative of the victim said he had met Pradeep shortly before the incident and learned about the attack after leaving the premises. “Pradeep was fine when I met him,” he said.Pradeep’s sister, Nisha, alleged that he was taken to hospital 30 minutes after the attack, and money was demanded to allow the family to see him.“He was killed with a knife. How did it get inside the jail?” she asked, adding that his next court hearing was approaching. The murder was premeditated, she alleged.Jail officials denied all allegations. They also dismissed the family’s claim that Pradeep was lodged in jail in a murder case.Delhi’s jails have seen several murders earlier too, including those of gangsters Ankit Gujjar and Tillu Tajpuria. Gujjar was killed on Aug 4, 2021, and Tajpuria on May 2, 2023.In 2018, a 22-year-old man was killed inside Rohini Jail by another inmate in a battle for dominance inside prison.
Article Summary: A 31-year-old undertrial was allegedly stabbed to death by two other inmates inside central jail no. 10 in Rohini Monday. The deceased has been identified as Pradeep alias Mohinder, who was in judicial custody. Tihar sources said he was involved in more than 10 cases.

Article Title: CM shielding MPSC chief, alleges Dipke; BJP hits back, says CJP founder daydreaming and acting as AAP agent
Article Text:
In photo: CJP Abhijeet Dipke, Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday accused chief minister Devendra Fadnavis of shielding Maharashtra Public Service Commission chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar amid growing allegations of irregularities. BJP dismissed Dipke’s claims as baseless “daydreaming” driven by political motives.“Was he made MPSC chairperson because he was your senior in college? Personal equations should remain private,” he said, targeting Fadnavis at a gathering of MPSC candidates in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, which organisers said was attended by around 2,000 aspirants.BJP spokesperson Sanjay Kenekar dismissed Dipke’s claims as “nothing but Mungerilal Ke Haseen Sapne,” accusing him of acting as an Aam Aadmi Party “agent.” “Fadnavis leads a govt that secured a clear electoral mandate,” he said.Dipke said confidence in MPSC had eroded and insisted that Bhimanwar’s removal was necessary to restore trust. “Aspirants have lost faith in MPSC. If question papers are being leaked repeatedly, students have no reason to trust the system. To rebuild confidence, the chairperson must be removed,” Dipke said.He said protests would continue till Bhimanwar resigned, questioning why he remained in office despite allegations raised by aspirants over the conduct of recruitment examinations.Highlighting the scale of the aspirants’ community, Dipke said nearly 20 lakh MPSC candidates and their families constituted a significant voter base. “If Bhimanwar is not made to resign, aspirants will not support you. Leave aside him, you could lose your own post,” he warned.In a statement issued later, CJP said Dipke had urged students to join the “Bhimanwar Should Resign” campaign by posting videos on social media outlining their concerns and demanding accountability from MPSC leadership.According to the party, the meeting focused on alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations and the need for accountability within the commission. Dipke had held a similar interaction with aspirants in Amravati on Sept 19, while another outreach meeting is planned in Nashik.The CJP statement also cited a March 2025 Loksatta report that raised questions over the procurement of radar equipment for interceptor vehicles during Bhimanwar’s tenure as Maharashtra transport commissioner. The allegations have, however, not established any criminal wrongdoing.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke accused chief minister Devendra Fadnavis of shielding Maharashtra Public Service Commission chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar. BJP dismissed Dipke’s claims as baseless “daydreaming” driven by political motives.

Article Title: Intruder shoots teacher dead inside UP school, kills himself
Article Text:
Police identified the victim as Nishat Fatima, a resident of Hidayat Nagar, and the attacker as Saud Ansari, 28, of Naurangabad.





MEERUT: A 26-year-old woman teacher was shot dead inside a private school in Lakhimpur Kheri on Monday by a 28-year-old man who entered the campus carrying a country-made pistol and later shot himself, triggering panic among around 350 students present at the time.The attack came barely seven weeks after a private-school teacher in Faridabad was stabbed repeatedly inside her campus by a man who had entered seeking her out.Police identified the victim as Nishat Fatima, a resident of Hidayat Nagar, and the attacker as Saud Ansari, 28, of Naurangabad.SSP Kheri Khyati Garg said Ansari reached Children’s Academy in Shahpura Kothi area around 11.30am, met Fatima and went upstairs with her before an argument broke out.“He took out a country-made pistol and fired three rounds at her at close range. He then shot himself. Both died on the spot,” Garg told TOI. Police said Fatima suffered fatal injuries to her head and upper body.Gunshots sent students and staff running for safety while examinations were under way.School management alerted police, who moved children away from the crime scene, cordoned off the corridor and called forensic teams.Investigators recovered four spent cartridges, one live cartridge and the country-made pistol.Police are now examining how Ansari entered the campus with a firearm, his movements inside the two-storey building and security arrangements at the school, including CCTV coverage and visitor-entry procedures.SSP added, “The accused had been forcing the victim to marry, as alleged by the woman’s family in the complaint. The victim’s brother, Shadab Akhter, has filed a complaint, following which an FIR has been filed against the accused Ansari under BNS section 103 (murder) and section 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) against Ansari’s parents. Shadab alleged that they had informed the parents that their son was harassing Fatima, but they didn’t take any action and, at their behest, he committed the crime. ”Ansari’s social media posts in the days before the shooting have also become part of the investigation. He had posted photographs with messages such as “Usse Bhool Ja” and, shortly before the attack, uploaded a longer note asking people to delete his photographs and messages after his death. “In this world nothing is permanent, no one is permanent. We came in this world so we have to leave this world for sure,” part of the post read.The incident echoed the Aug 3 Faridabad school killing, when a masked 21-year-old man entered a private school in Sikrona, sought out teacher Sandhya Karhana and stabbed her more than 30 times in roughly 30 seconds after dragging her from the classroom area. The attack, captured on CCTV, had similarly raised questions over how an armed outsider could enter a school and reach a teacher during working hours.
Article Summary: A 26-year-old woman teacher was shot dead inside a private school in Lakhimpur Kheri on Monday. Police identified the victim as Nishat Fatima, a resident of Hidayat Nagar, and the attacker as Saud Ansari, 28, of Naurangabad. Ansari entered the campus carrying a country-made pistol and later shot himself.

Article Title: Stalked for a year, blackmailed with private photos: 16-year-old 'raped' in Gwalior
Article Text:
A 16-year-old girl was allegedly raped by her 17-year-old neighbor in Gwalior (Representative image)





BHOPAL: On the day two Class 10 students were allegedly harassed on a road in Bihar’s Jamui, a similar incident unfolded nearly 1,000 km away in Gwalior, where a 16-year-old girl was allegedly raped by her 17-year-old neighbour after he threatened and blackmailed her with private photographs, police said.The Gwalior girl was on her way to a coaching class on Saturday evening when the accused allegedly intercepted her on a motorcycle, threatened to make the photographs and chats public and forced her to accompany him to a flat.Police said the girl alleged that the accused raped her at the flat and later dropped her near her coaching centre.The accused had allegedly been stalking and harassing the Class 10 student for nearly a year, according to her complaint.The girl told police that he had repeatedly followed her to and from coaching classes and later began threatening her with private photographs and chat screenshots.According to the complaint, the harassment had briefly stopped after her family counselled her, but the accused allegedly resumed it.On Saturday around 6 pm, he allegedly intercepted her while she was going to coaching and threatened to circulate the photographs if she did not comply.After the alleged assault, the girl returned home and told her mother about the incident. Her family subsequently approached police, following which an FIR was registered late Sunday night under the POCSO Act and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Police traced the accused and took him into custody within hours. As he is also a minor, he was produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and sent to a reform home.“The accused is also a 17-year-old minor. He was taken into custody after being booked following the survivor’s complaint and was produced before court, which sent him to a reform home,” Gwalior Kotwali police station in-charge Prashant Sharma told TOI.Police said they were investigating the allegations and recording statements of relevant witnesses. They are also examining the digital material referred to in the complaint.(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: The Gwalior girl was on her way to a coaching class on Saturday evening. The accused allegedly intercepted her on a motorcycle, threatened to make the photographs and chats public and forced her to accompany him to a flat. The girl alleged that the accused raped her at the flat and later dropped her near her coaching centre.

Article Title: ‘This is residential society, not hotel’: Airbnb-style daily rentals spark protest by Ghaziabad’s Windsor Park residents
Article Text:
Residents protested alleged short-term rentals and commercial activities within their society.

What is Airbnb?

‘Safety is at risk because of outsiders’ movement’

Residents question RWA functioning

Residents seek action from authorities

Uttar Pradesh Homestay and B&B Policy 2025

RWA says it does not support Airbnb activities





GHAZIABAD: Residents of Vaibhav Khand Windsor Park Society took to the streets on Sunday to protest against the alleged conversion of residential flats into Airbnb-style short-term rental units, claiming that the constant movement of outsiders was affecting the atmosphere and raising security concerns for families.Residents staged a peaceful protest near Gate No. 1, holding posters and raising slogans against the RWA. They submitted a joint complaint to the District Magistrate, Police Commissioner, GDA, Nagar Nigam and Tourism Department, seeking an independent investigation into the alleged activities.Airbnb is an online platform that allows people to rent rooms, apartments and other properties for short stays. Depending on the listing, these stays can range from a few days to shorter periods.Residents alleged that flats in the society were being offered to outsiders on a daily or short-term basis. They questioned the practice particularly in the studio apartments in Towers A and B. According to residents, the two towers have around 270 studio apartments, while the society has around 770 flats in total.Protesters alleged that dozens of flats were being occupied by people on daily or short-term rentals and claimed that, in some cases, occupants were staying without police verification and necessary registration.Residents said the movement of unknown people had become a concern for families living in the society.Amit Gera, who participated in the protest, alleged that flats in the Kabana Tower studio apartments were being rented out on a daily basis and even for a few hours, affecting the security of the society. He said it was necessary to keep a check on the movement of unknown people.Raina said residents should not be allowed to rent out rooms for a few hours within the society.Sadhna Mishra said, “This is a residential society, not a hotel.”Residents also alleged that some occupants of short-stay flats created a ruckus late at night. Complaints included alleged alcohol consumption inside vehicles in the parking area, verbal abuse and physical altercations.Protesters further alleged that bottles had been thrown from windows and that women and girls had faced lewd comments. Residents cited a recent FIR concerning a young woman who was allegedly found unconscious and injured in flat B-1001 and questioned the security arrangements in the society.The circumstances of that incident and whether it was connected to any short-term rental activity are subject to investigation.Protesters questioned the functioning of RWA president Reena Patnaik and secretary Vineet Garg. They alleged that commercial rental activities were being encouraged through alleged collusion between some individuals associated with the RWA and property operators.Some residents also alleged that individuals associated with the secretary were purchasing or renting apartments and subsequently offering them for short-term rentals. These allegations have not been independently confirmed.Residents said that despite complaints, the RWA had not put in place a clear policy or taken effective action against the alleged activities.Residents have sent complaints to the District Magistrate, Police Commissioner, GDA vice-president and Tourism Department, seeking their intervention.They demanded that flats allegedly operating without the required registration and police character certificates under thebe investigated and that action be taken if violations are found.Residents also demanded that such flats be closed or sealed, if necessary. They have asked the RWA to provide details of tenants, rent agreements and police verification records.RWA president Reena Patnaik said that, according to the information available to her, no Airbnb-like activities were being carried out in the society.She said the RWA had never supported such activities and that a board prohibiting Airbnb had also been installed on the premises.Patnaik said that if a complaint against any flat was received along with concrete evidence, and police action required the RWA’s cooperation, the association would provide full support.Residents who participated in the protest included Amit Gera, Alok Lal, Rajiv Kumar Jain, Shobhit Tyagi, Megha Dey, SP Arya, Ravi Tanuja, Rajiv Verma, Nidhi Jain, Sagar Gulati, Mohit Agarwal, Bhuvnesh Pandey, Piyush Mishra, Narendra Chaudhary, Raina Dixit, Sadhna Mishra, Sandeep Mishra, Shalini Saxena, Sanjeev Saxena, Shalini Khurana, Vandana Gera, Shweta Singh, Manish Sinha, Ravi Arora, Avinash, Deepak Dhawan and Ankit Verma, among other residents.Residents warned that if the issue was not resolved soon, they would expand the protest.
Article Summary: Residents of Vaibhav Khand Windsor Park Society took to the streets on Sunday to protest against the alleged conversion of residential flats into Airbnb-style short-term rental units. Residents staged a peaceful protest near Gate No. 1, holding posters and raising slogans against the RWA. They submitted a joint complaint to the District Magistrate, Police Commissioner, GDA, Nagar Nigam and Tourism Department, seeking an independent investigation.

Article Title: Mumbai Coastal Road tragedy: BMW driver had faced 2 prior cases over drunken brawl, speeding
Article Text:
Mumbai Costal road incident on Sunday





MUMBAI: Shanay Gajjar, the 21-year-old student who was driving the BMW that plunged 70 feet down from the Coastal Road flyover early Sunday near Lotus Jetty, and who died in the fatal mishap along with two others, previously faced two cases registered by the city police. In March, Gamdevi police registered a case against him for alleged dangerous driving and endangering the lives of others. Last month, Bandra police filed a case against him and three of his friends for allegedly engaging in a drunken brawl with police outside a pub.On Sunday, the BMW was travelling from Marine Drive towards Haji Ali on the northbound carriageway when the tragedy occurred. Police identified the deceased as Dhairya Sheth (17), Aditya Jaskania (19) and Shanay Gajjar, who was driving the car that belonged to his family. Aditya Oswal (23), who suffered multiple injuries in the accident, is in the hospital.Tardeo police on Monday registered a case against Gajjar for causing death by negligence, rash driving and dangerous driving. All the victims were from Ahmedabad.CCTV footage showed the BMW speeding. The impact was such that one of the victi­ms was thrown around 20 feet from the car and another was found outside it. Police said Ga­­jjar was still partly inside the vehicle, with his leg on the accelerator.In Aug, Bandra police had filed a case against Gajjar and his three friends for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of public functions and under the Maharashtra Prohibition Act. They were served notices and allowed to leave. Police are yet to file a chargesheet in the case.Police constable Baban Sagare alleged the four were caught fighting after partying at a pub on the night of Aug 19-20. They initially left after police intervened, but later began to argue among themselves on the road. Police alleged that after they intervened again, under the influence of alcohol, the four argued with the cops and then charged at them when asked to leave. All four were taken to Bandra police station, where they allegedly caused a disturbance, and later at Bhabha Hospital where they were taken for medical tests. A police officer said they refused the medical examination and blood tests, and the medical officer recorded their refusal.Earlier, on March 29, Omkar Shirke (29), a businessman and resident of Tardeo in central Mumbai, lodged an FIR against the driver of a BMW car bearing the number DD 01 C 6302. Shirke told police that on the night of March 28, while he was going towards his residence, a speeding BMW passed by dangerously close to him. He later spotted the car near Mahalaxmi temple and questioned the driver who gave evasive replies. Police then issued a notice to Gajjar. A case was registered against him under Motor Vehicles Act’s Section 184 (driving dangerously) and BNS’s sections 125 (an act endangering life or personal safety of others) and 281 (rash driving or riding on a public way).
Article Summary: Shanay Gajjar, 21, was driving the BMW that plunged 70 feet down from the Coastal Road flyover early Sunday near Lotus Jetty. In March, Gamdevi police registered a case against him for alleged dangerous driving and endangering the lives of others. Last month, Bandra police filed a case. against him and three of his friends for allegedly engaging in a drunken brawl with police outside a pub.

Article Title: Speeding car rams into 19-year-old, constable, 3 others in Mumbai; driver and bizman booked
Article Text:
The constable alleged the businessman, seated in the rear, gesturedthe driver to drive away when he tried to stop the vehicle





MUMBAI: A speeding electric crossover utility vehicle rammed into a 19-year-old college girl, who survived the incident with injuries, and struck several people, including a police constable, and three stationary autorickshaws in Khar West early on Sunday.Khar police arrested driver Dinesh Yadav (36), a Goregaon resident, and charged vehicle owner Mehul Joshi (50), a businessman from Malad West. An FIR was registered, after which Yadav was put in police custody, while Joshi was served a notice and asked to appear for questioning when summoned.The accident occurred around 1.35am near Social Bar on Khar Station Road. Police said the vehicle first knocked down Stacia Pereira (19), who was standing beside the road, and ran over her.“Joshi, who was returning home after partying in Khar and was seated in the rear, claimed Yadav had suffered a seizure. However, constable Sanjay Sanap alleged that Joshi gestured to Yadav to drive away and pushed the constable when he tried to stop the vehicle and help those injured,” said a Khar police officer.Police said they were awaiting Yadav’s medical report to verify the seizure claim.TOI is in possession of the FIR that named the driver and the businessman as accused in the case.Sanap said the vehicle passed over Pereira before hitting his vehicle, two to three autorickshaws and other people. It eventually stopped after striking an autorickshaw.“With help from bystanders, police pushed the car back and pulled Pereira from underneath. She suffered severe injuries to her waist, hands and legs and was unable to move. Autorickshaw driver Asarfi Shrichand Mohto (30) suffered a shoulder injury, while his vehicle was damaged. Shanay Bhosle and Shrivats Palepu suffered minor injuries,” said Sanap in the FIR.Pereira was taken to Bhabha Hospital, where she is undergoing treatment. Her parents were subsequently informed.Meanwhile, the police team seized the CUV car and took the driver and the businessman to the police station before they were charged with the offence.
Article Summary: A speeding electric crossover utility vehicle rammed into a 19-year-old college girl, who survived the incident with injuries. The vehicle also struck several people, including a police constable, and three stationary autorickshaws in Khar West early on Sunday. Police said the vehicle first knocked down Stacia Pereira (19), who was standing beside the road, and ran over her.

Article Title: 2 infants die after fire breaks out at Telangana's RIMS hospital; 28 newborns rescued
Article Text:
five-day-old newborn sadly lost their life due to a fire that broke out at RIMS hospital





HYDERABAD: Two infants, including a five-day-old baby, died after a fire broke out at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Adilabad late Monday night.Officials said at least 25 other newborns were evacuated from the ward and shifted to safety. They were in stable condition.According to officials, the fire broke out around 11.50pm while the children and their attendants were inside the unit.They added that preliminary investigations indicated that an electrical short circuit in a window air conditioner may have triggered the blaze. The exact cause of the fire, however, is yet to be established.The SNCU is a hospital ward that provides round-the-clock care for sick, premature or low-birth-weight newborns who need extra medical attention.Adilabad station fire officer D Jayatram told TOI that the children were present in the ward when the fire broke out. “The fire appears to have originated from the AC due to a short circuit. The ward quickly filled with smoke, and the children were evacuated. While one infant is believed to have died due to asphyxiation, the other one passed away while undergoing treatment,” he added.Some of the attendants present in the ward were affected by smoke inhalation. A fire tender was rushed to the spot, while district authorities and police also reached the hospital in the early hours of Tuesday. Police registered a case and launched an investigation into the incident.Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy and health minister Damodar Rajanarasimha expressed grief over the deaths. The CM also ordered an inquiry into the incident. He directed officials to submit a report on the cause of the fire and asked them to ensure the best possible treatment for the children undergoing treatment while closely monitoring their health.
Article Summary: Two infants, including a five-day-old baby, died after a fire broke out at the Special Newborn Care Unit (SNCU) of Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) in Adilabad late Monday night. At least 25 other newborns were evacuated from the ward and shifted to safety.

Article Title: IIT Bombay student suicide: Welfare reforms, mental health focus sought; security beefed up - top developments
Article Text:
The student said Prof Doolla’s removal as Dean was “completely wrong”, asserting that he was only doing his job.

(With agency inputs)





MUMBAI: Students at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay have demanded changes to the institute’s student welfare system and greater focus on mental health, following concerns raised in the wake of the Sahil Wakode suicide case.Security was beefed up outside the IIT-Bombay campus on Tuesday.They also said that targeting one professor over the case was "completely wrong".Wakode, 22, a second-year BTech student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, was found hanging from the ceiling fan in his hostel room at IIT Bombay’s Powai campus on the evening of September 18.He was allegedly caught using a mobile phone to access ChatGPT during a mid-semester examination earlier that day.The incident triggered protests by students on the campus.The Mumbai Police have booked Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, who has been removed as the dean of Administrative Affairs, under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Section 108 (abetment of suicide) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, following a complaint lodged by Sahil's family."Even if students differ on the issue, we all agree on one thing: changes need to be brought in student welfare, including the wellness cell, psychiatrist support, and similar areas.Students' voices should be heard when decisions are made," a student told news agency PTI on Monday."But, I think students disagree on the treatment of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla. The caste angle portrayed in the media is wrong and does not exist," he asserted.The student said Prof Doolla’s removal as Dean (Administrative Affairs) was “completely wrong”, asserting that he was only doing his job.Another student told the media that reports of caste discrimination were incorrect."There is no discrimination on the basis of caste in the institute. Therefore, the media reports on caste bias in IIT Bombay are completely wrong," he said.Another student said stress might have led Sahil Wakode to take the extreme step."I feel stress must be the reason; otherwise there is no such other reason that could have led Wakode to take such a step. But stress is there because the courses are difficult. I feel that is a part of engineering, and that is how you learn," he said.However, some students also alleged that Prof Doolla had a track record of suspending students over what they described as trivial reasons and removing them from hostels.Measures taken during Prof Doolla's tenure as Dean of Students Affairs had created a sense of fear, they claimed, adding that his past record made them believe he could have ordered suspension if they had spoken of it following the incident.IIT Bombay on Monday removed Prof Doolla as Dean (Administrative Affairs) following protests by students and political activists over Sahil Wakode’s suicide. Doolla, however, continues to serve as a faculty member.The institute also issued a public apology for its earlier communication, which characterised the events leading up to the student’s death before a detailed inquiry had been completed."In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding Sahil's demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process," it said in a statement, retracting its earlier assertion that Sahil was caught cheating but faced no disciplinary action.However, student groups expressed dissatisfaction with the move, demanding his suspension as a faculty member.On Monday evening, faculty members held a march on the IIT Bombay campus in support of Doolla. The Faculty Forum said Doolla had followed the “Senate-approved exam procedure” when he reported Sahil for allegedly using a phone during the September 18 examination.Sahil’s father, Ravindra Wakode, however, alleged that his son was mocked, tortured and discriminated against on caste lines. He also demanded a probe into the role of the IIT Bombay administration in his son’s death.
Article Summary: Security was beefed up outside the IIT-Bombay campus on Tuesday. They also said that targeting one professor over the case was "completely wrong" Sahil Wakode, 22, was found hanging from the ceiling fan in his hostel room.

Article Title: 2 videos, 20 minutes, 3 arrests: How a Class X girl was harassed on camera in Bihar's Jamui
Article Text:
A disturbing case emerged in Jamui, Bihar, where a Class X girl was harassed and molested by a group of youths





PATNA: In an incident that has brought Bihar's law and order under the spotlight again, a Class X girl was subjected to harassment and molestation on the road by a group of youths in Jamui district, who also recorded the act on camera.As video clips of the act went viral, triggering a storm, police detained three perpetrators, all minors, on Monday.The horror unfolded on Saturday when the girl had gone to Marwa Pahad, a scenic hill, along with a male classmate on a scooter after attending coaching classes.While the two were returning, a group stopped and surrounded them. They allegedly forced them off the scooter and started questioning and abusing them.The videos show the youth harassing the girl and touching her inappropriately. Her friend was manhandled, too. As the two tried to run away, they were chased and roughed up.Their ordeal allegedly lasted 15-20 minutes before the two students managed to flee the spot.Two video clips of the harassment went viral on Monday, sparking an outrage and prompting police to initiate action."The girl and her friend were traced and their statements were recorded.After receiving a written complaint from the girl, an FIR was registered. All the youths visible in the videos have been identified," Jamui SP Vishwajit Dayal said.The SP constituted an SIT, headed by SDPO Deepti Monali, to conduct a probe. She said based on the video footage, seven-eight persons were booked under various sections of BNS and Pocso Act. While three of them were taken into custody, raids were being carried out to apprehend the others, she added.Police are also taking steps to remove the videos uploaded on social media, officials said.Police are also scrutinising the criminal records, if any, of the accused and analysing the videos and other available evidence to establish the role of each person involved. Opposition members, including Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav, launched an attack on Samrat Choudhary govt, while BJP members pushed back against charges of lawlessness.The NCW and state women's commission also took cognisance of the incident. NCW chairperson Vijaya Rahatkar wrote to Bihar DGP, seeking action against the accused and a detailed action-taken report within seven days.
Article Summary: The horror unfolded on Saturday when the girl had gone to Marwa Pahad, a scenic hill, along with a male classmate on a scooter after attending coaching classes. As video clips of the act went viral, triggering a storm, police detained three perpetrators, all minors, on Monday.

However, Neeraj succumbed to his injuries during treatment, while his wife continues to receive medical care.
