Article Title: Surendra Koli autopsy held back as doctors probe blood around nose, mouth
Article Text:
Police maintained that initial findings pointed to suicide but said they would wait for the autopsy and forensic evidence before reaching a conclusion





DEHRADUN: Haridwar police were still awaiting Surendra Koli’s post-mortem report on Monday, three days after he was found dead inside his newly opened tea stall, as a two-doctor panel had yet to determine what caused blood around his nose and mouth.Koli’s family cited the blood marks to allege foul play and sought a high-level probe, while police maintained that initial findings pointed to suicide but said they would wait for the autopsy and forensic evidence before reaching a conclusion.The doctors conducted the post-mortem for around three hours on Saturday under videography but held back the report pending a clearer medical opinion.“The post-mortem was completed, but doctors have not yet concluded what caused the bleeding from his nose and mouth. His family has cited the same blood marks while alleging murder,” a police officer privy to the investigation told TOI.Koli’s younger brother Anand had told TOIon Saturday, “We saw blood under his nose and mouth, which adds to our suspicion.”His elder brother Chandan, who saw the body before the post-mortem and later attended the last rites in Haridwar, submitted a complaint at Saptarishi police outpost seeking a detailed probe.Family members also pointed to bloodstains around the face while questioning the initial suicide theory.Police, however, said they had so far found no evidence establishing homicide.SI Khemendra Gangwar, who is probing the death, told TOI, “initial findings point towards suicide, but we are waiting for the post-mortem report to establish the exact cause of death. Doctors are taking time before finalising it, and we expect the report in the next couple of days.”Investigators were also examining CCTV footage from the Saptarishi-Bhupatwala area to reconstruct Koli’s movements before his death.Police found no suicide note at the stall, though they recovered a diary containing what appeared to be daily expenses and work-related entries.Koli had started selling tea and biscuits from the rented stall only a few days before his death and had also been living there.After walking out of jail in Nov 2025 following his acquittal in the last of 13 Nithari cases, he had spent several months in Haridwar, taking up security and labour work before trying to start the tea business.
Article Summary: Surendra Koli was found dead inside his newly opened tea stall in Haridwar. His family cited the blood marks to allege foul play and sought a high-level probe. Police said they would wait for the autopsy and forensic evidence before reaching a conclusion.

Article Title: Punjab woman gets loan after 3 years of death; FIR filed
Article Text:
(AI image) A deceased woman's identity was used for a loan in 2022. Forged documents, including another woman's photograph, facilitated this fraud





MOHALI: A woman who died in Nov 2019 allegedly “came alive” in official records three years later when a Rs 40,000 loan was sanctioned in her name using forged documents, including the photograph of another woman, in Nihal Singh Wala.The Punjab State Crime Cell, Mohali, registered a case against five people following a fact-finding inquiry by the Punjab Bureau of Investigation and crime zone Bathinda into an alleged loan fraud using fake documents and identities.According to the inquiry, Shubh Lakshmi Private Finance Limited sanctioned the Rs 40,000 loan in 2022 in the name of the woman who had died in 2019. Investigators found that another woman’s photograph was allegedly used in the loan documents.The inquiry flagged two other alleged instances of loan fraud. In one, a Rs 40,000 loan was sanctioned using a woman’s documents, with around Rs 36,000 later deposited in a bank account. In another, a woman allegedly used another woman’s documents to obtain a loan.
Article Summary: A deceased woman's identity was used for a loan in 2022. Forged documents, including another woman's photograph, facilitated this fraud. The Punjab State Crime Cell, Mohali, registered a case against five people following a fact- finding inquiry by the Punjab Bureau of Investigation.

Article Title: Yavatmal in shock, IIT-Bombay student’s kin seek CID probe; allege boy’s death was not suicide
Article Text:
The family’s allegations of caste-based discrimination, psychological pressure or humiliating treatment at the institute have not been independently established.





YAVATMAL: The family of 19-year-old Sahil Ravindra Wakode, a second-year student at IIT Bombay , has demanded a CID investigation into his death at the institute hostel, alleging that the incident was not a suicide.Wakode’s family alleged foul play and submitted a letter to the district administration in Yavatmal seeking a probe. While his parents have left for Mumbai to follow up on the case, relatives back home set up banners outside the family’s home demanding justice for Sahil.His aunt Ganga Wakode rejected the suicide theory. “Sahil could never have taken his life,” she said. Ganga said Sahil was intelligent, focused and composed since childhood and committed to his academic goals, making it difficult for them to accept that he would take such a drastic step.Ganga also questioned the institute’s handling of an alleged mobile phone incident during an examination, asking how Sahil could have used a phone inside an IIT hall where phones are prohibited. The family said the institute should have informed his parents had any such incident occurred.The family’s allegations of caste-based discrimination, psychological pressure or humiliating treatment at the institute have not been independently established.No response from IIT Bombay or the district administration on the CID demand was available.Sahil, a second-year student from Shelu Brahmanwada village in Arni taluka, scored 94 percentile in JEE Advanced, ranking 614th nationally in the Scheduled Caste category. He reportedly achieved an 8.5 CGPA in his first year at IIT Bombay and was a Mathematics Olympiad gold medallist.
Article Summary: Sahil Ravindra Wakode, a second-year student at IIT Bombay, died at the institute hostel. His family alleged foul play and submitted a letter to the district administration in Yavatmal seeking a probe. His aunt Ganga Wakode rejected the suicide theory. “Sahil could never have taken his life,” she said.

Article Title: 91-year-old woman dies after monkey attacks, pushes her in Karnataka
Article Text:
CCTV footage showed the monkey attacking the elderly woman.





KARNATAKA: A 91-year-old woman died on Monday after allegedly being attacked and pushed by a monkey in BT Patil Nagar in Karnataka’s Koppal district.The deceased was identified as Najamunisa Begum.The incident occurred when she was standing outside her house, where the monkey reportedly attacked and pushed her, leaving her seriously injured.Begum was rushed to a hospital for treatment following the incident.CCTV footage showed the monkey attacking the elderly woman.However, she later succumbed to her injuries.The circumstances surrounding the monkey attack are being looked into.
Article Summary: A 91-year-old woman died on Monday after allegedly being attacked and pushed by a monkey. The incident occurred in BT Patil Nagar in Karnataka’s Koppal district. The circumstances surrounding the monkey attack are being looked into.

Article Title: Another hit-and-run in Delhi-NCR: Man collecting birthday cake hit by speeding SUV in Greater Noida, suffers spine fracture
Article Text:
A speeding car struck a pedestrian near Ek Murti Chowk, causing serious injuries





NOIDA: A 32-year-old man suffered several fractures in a hit-and-run accident at Ek Murti Chowk in Greater Noida earlier this month. A video of the accident recorded by a rear-view camera of a car shows that the collision impact flung the man into the air.Police have arrested the driver, a 24-year-old management student, on Sept 14 and impounded the car.According to a complaint filed by the victim, Himanshu Rai, at the Bisrakh police station, the accident took place at around 4.35 am on Sept 5. He told the cops, “It was my birthday, so after work my wife and I had gone out.”He collected a pre-ordered cake from a bakery and was crossing the road at the chowk when a white SUV, driven at high speed, rammed him.“The car hit me at what appeared to be a speed of over 100 km per hour and drove away. The way the car was being driven, it seemed that the driver might have been under the influence of alcohol,” he said.People in the vicinity rushed to his aid and took him to a hospital for treatment.The man sustained fractures to his legs, hand and knees, besides suffering a fracture to his spine. He is currently undergoing treatment at the hospital.Police subsequently traced the vehicle and initiated action against the driver, Priyanshu. The Tata Punch allegedly involved in the accident was taken into custody.A case has been registered against him under BNS sections 125(b) (act endangering life or personal safety) and 281 (rash driving).The accident comes at the heel of a hit and run incident in Gurgaon where a biker was chased down by a group of men on Golf Course Road.Kalyan Bainsla (33), who rammed his car into Shivani Chauhan’s bike and caused her to fall in the middle of fast-moving traffic on Golf Course Road Sunday morning, was arrested at Dausa in Rajasthan on Tuesday.A video from her bike’s camera that Chauhan uploaded online showed her being knocked down near Sector 55-56 Rapid Metro station after the car repeatedly tried to get alongside her bike.Her Aprilia RS 457 slid across the road, while traffic sped past her.Bainsla’s cousin Lovneesh (32), who was in the Maruti Ciaz with him on Sunday, was arrested too. After examining the video of the crash that Shivani shared, police have added the attempt to murder charge in the FIR against Bainsla.“He caused the collision deliberately from the side. He had an intention to kill her,” DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar said
Article Summary: A 32-year-old man suffered several fractures in a hit-and-run accident at Ek Murti Chowk in Greater Noida earlier this month. A video of the accident recorded by a rear-view camera of a car shows that the collision impact flung the man into the air. The incident comes at the heel of a hit and run incident in Gurgaon where a biker was chased down.

Article Title: Thousands of US flights grounded for hours across major US airports, here's why
Article Text:
Thousands of US flights grounded : What went wrong

Government’s response

Airports and flights affected

Services restored

US travellers faced a tough situation when thousands of flights across United States were stopped on September 21 after a telecommunications outage. As reported by Reuters, the outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to halt arrivals at major East Coast airports. The report further reveals that the service disruption began around 9.45 am when constructions workers accidentally severed a telecom line in New Jersey which led to crippling of communications at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility. Many incoming flights were stopped at all the three major New York-area airports including JFK, LaGuardia, and Newark and Philadelphia, Boston, and two smaller New York-area airports due to the outage. The telecommunications outage lasted for around eight hours and led to widespread cancellation and flight diversions.As per the Reuters report, the trouble began around 9:45 a.m. when workers accidentally cut a telecom line the FAA relies on. The disruption forced the agency to halt incoming flights at all three major New York-area airports, along with Philadelphia, Boston, and two smaller New York-area airports.The problem wasn't fully resolved for roughly eight hours.According to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford, the outage traced back to a failed circuit at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility that handles traffic for the affected airports. When controllers tried switching to the backup system, they discovered the backup fiber line had also been damaged — a break Bedford said would take roughly 13 hours to fix on its own. A new circuit was being installed in the meantime to restore service faster.Initial blame shifted more than once through the day. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy first pointed to an Amtrak construction crew, saying it had accidentally cut into a fiber line near New Brunswick, New Jersey. Amtrak pushed back, denying responsibility. New Jersey Transit later said one of its own crews had been digging about 10 feet from utility markings at a nearby work site, and said it was still trying to determine whether Verizon or a contractor was responsible for those markings in the first place. Verizon confirmed it was working to repair the damaged cable and restore connectivity.The numbers were staggering. Flight-tracking site FlightAware reported around 7,000 flights delayed or canceled nationwide, including 1,400 flights at the three major New York-area airports alone. Newark Liberty International — a major hub for United Airlines — was hit hardest, with more than half of all flights there canceled; United issued a travel waiver to help affected passengers. More than 100 flights were diverted to other airports altogether.Reagan Washington National Airport also briefly paused flights for over an hour due to volume issues, and Philadelphia saw a second ground stop before flights resumed later in the afternoon. Boston's ground stop, triggered by spillover traffic from the other closures, was eventually lifted as well.By around 5:30 p.m., New Jersey Transit said most of the fiber cables had been repaired and were coming back online.
Article Summary: Thousands of flights across United States were stopped on September 21 after a telecommunications outage. The outage forced the Federal Aviation Administration to halt arrivals at major East Coast airports. The trouble began around 9:45 a.m. when workers accidentally cut a telecom line the FAA relies on. The problem wasn't fully resolved for roughly eight hours.
